classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate shared results across four equations while using every digit once, choosing a viable multiplication triple and testing compatible remaining digit pairs.

content.prompt: Place the numbers 1 to 9 in the circles to make each of the equations true.

spec.description: Nine blank circles arranged in three aligned rows. Horizontal subtraction, division and addition equations intersect a vertical multiplication equation in the rightmost column. The vertical equality sign is rotated.
spec.mathematics: For rows (a,b,c), (d,e,f), (g,h,i): a-b=c, d/e=f, g+h=i and c*f=i; use each integer 1 through 9 once.
spec.answerVisibility: All nine interiors remain blank in the student edition.

answer.short:
Top row: $9-5=4$.

Middle row: $6\div3=2$.

Bottom row: $7+1=8$.

Right column: $4\times2=8$.
answer.worked:
Choose $4\times2=8$ for the right column. The remaining digits are $1,3,5,6,7,9$.

Using each remaining digit once gives:
$$\begin{align*}9-5&=4\\6\div3&=2\\7+1&=8\end{align*}$$
The right column also checks: $4\times2=8$. Every number from 1 to 9 appears once.
